stories.headline: Xi's Washington visit ends with eight US-China deliverables, an AI dialogue and a $30B tariff cut

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping's state visit to the US ran September 23-25, and China's foreign ministry published a list of eight 'deliverables and understandings' reached with Trump.
key_facts.excerpt: From September 23 to 25 local time, President Xi Jinping paid a state visit to the United States... and reached eight deliverables and understandings

key_facts.fact: The two sides agreed to set up a China-U.S. AI Dialogue, with the next exchange in November 2026, plus a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents.
key_facts.excerpt: The two sides agree on the establishment of the China-U.S. AI Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI. The next exchange will occur in November 2026. China and the U.S. also agree to establish a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents.

key_facts.fact: The leaders endorsed a US$30 billion reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement and a new Board of Trade mechanism; the militaries agreed to conclude a crisis-communication memorandum as soon as possible.
key_facts.excerpt: establishing and taking forward the Board of Trade and other mechanisms, reaching an arrangement for a US$30 billion reciprocal tariff reduction... the Chinese and U.S. militaries agree to conclude a memorandum of understanding on crisis communication and prevention

key_facts.fact: On Iran, Xi and Trump agreed Tehran should honor its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons and that no country should charge transit fees on international waterways.
key_facts.excerpt: On Iran, Xi and Trump have agreed that Tehran should fulfill its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons. No country or institution shall charge transit fees for passage through international waterways, they said.

key_facts.fact: There was no joint statement; the outcomes omitted rare-earth exports and any easing of US curbs on advanced semiconductors, and Beijing had hoped for a longer truce than the extension to January 10.
key_facts.excerpt: There was no mention of increasing exports of China's rare earth minerals to the US nor was there any indication that restrictions on advanced US semiconductors would be eased.

key_facts.fact: On Monday China's commerce ministry listed proposed tariff cuts on US farm goods from corn to dairy, while the US will reduce levies on Chinese toys, fireworks and Christmas ornaments; analysts called the summit a 'managed stalemate'.
key_facts.excerpt: China has proposed cutting tariffs on a range of US agricultural goods, from corn to dairy, a commerce ministry list showed on Monday. In return, the US will reduce levies on Chinese imports such as toys, fireworks and Christmas ornaments.

stories.headline: Trump rejects Iran's 7-day offer to reopen Hormuz; Brent rebounds above $106

key_facts.fact: Iran offered, via Qatari mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, releasing frozen funds and ending attacks on all fronts.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran projected a message of defiance while also proposing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if its seven conditions were met. They included lifting the blockade on Iran, the release of frozen Iranian funds and an end to attacks on all fronts

key_facts.fact: Trump publicly rejected the proposal on Saturday, September 26: 'I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they're losing so badly.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump publicly rejected the proposal on Saturday. The plan would have reopened the strait within seven days and resumed nuclear negotiations in return for measures including lifting the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

key_facts.fact: On Sunday a Guards-linked outlet reported a sea-launched cruise missile was fired at a vessel using an unauthorized route in the strait; Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said Tehran was 'fully prepared for the war to be resumed'.
key_facts.excerpt: A sea-launched cruise missile was fired at a vessel traveling along an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, local sources were quoted as saying by the Revolutionary Guards-affiliated Fars news agency sunday evening.

key_facts.fact: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said oil flows through the strait average nearly 13 million barrels a day, with one day last week topping 20 million barrels, above pre-conflict levels.
key_facts.excerpt: "There was a day just this last week where over 20 million barrels of oil, more than pre-conflict levels, flowed out of the strait," Wright told Fox News. The current average was "almost 13 million barrels a day," he added.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Bessent said Turkey and Oman stopped Mahan Air flights, the UAE halted Iranian airline flights, and major Turkish and UAE banks stopped transactions with Iran after US pressure.
key_facts.excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that Turkey and Oman had stopped Mahan Air flights, the UAE had halted flights by Iranian airlines and major banks in Turkey and the UAE had stopped transactions with Iran following US pressure.

key_facts.fact: Brent had settled Friday at $104.32 (down more than 2%) on hopes of a deal; after the rejection it rose $1.82 to $106.14 in early Monday trading, with WTI at $93.55.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures rose $1.82, or 1.74%, to $106.14 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $93.55 a barrel, up $1.14, or 1.23%.

stories.headline: SpaceX's Starship reaches orbit for the first time, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites

key_facts.fact: Starship lifted off from Starbase, Texas at 8:48 a.m. EDT (12:48 GMT) on September 28 on Flight 14, its 14th test flight and the third with the Version 3 vehicle.
key_facts.excerpt: Starship lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas today at 8:48 a.m. EDT (1248 GMT; 7:48 a.m. local Texas time), kicking off its 14th test flight to date.

key_facts.fact: One of the ship's engines shut down prematurely and SpaceX initially said it could not reach orbit, but reversed course minutes later and completed the orbital insertion burn.
key_facts.excerpt: one of Starship's three main engines shut down prematurely, a development that led SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot to announce on the company's live stream of the mission that the craft would be unable to reach orbit. But Huot reversed course minutes later

key_facts.fact: Starship deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites at roughly 269 km altitude; SpaceX says each handles 10 times more data than the V2 mini satellites launched on Falcon 9.
key_facts.excerpt: Once in orbit, Starship deployed 26 next-generation Starlink satellites one by one at an altitude of roughly 269 km (161 miles)... the V3 Starlink satellites on Monday's mission can handle 10 times more data than their predecessor V2 mini-sats

key_facts.fact: The mission, planned as six orbits over about 10 hours, was cut to roughly three hours, with splashdown moved north of Hawaii.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX said the spacecraft would reenter over the Pacific and splash down north of Hawaii three hours after blasting off from Texas. The company had been aiming for a 10-hour flight, spanning six full laps around Earth

key_facts.fact: The flight is meant to prove Starship's readiness for NASA's Artemis moon program; the 26 new satellites join about 11,000 older Starlinks already in service.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX launched its enormous Starship into orbit for the first time Monday, aiming for six full laps around Earth to prove its readiness for NASA's Artemis moon program... carried 26 of the latest and most advanced Starlink satellites to join the 11,000 older models

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk posted: 'First orbital flight of Starship successful!'
key_facts.excerpt: "First orbital flight of Starship successful!" SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on SpaceX's X platform.

stories.headline: FDA approves AbbVie's Juvmo (tavapadon), first D1/D5 dopamine agonist for Parkinson's

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved AbbVie's tavapadon, a next-generation dopamine agonist for Parkinson's disease, on September 25; it will be sold as Juvmo.
key_facts.excerpt: US FDA approves AbbVie's drug for Parkinson's disease... Published on 09/26/2026 at 03:31 am IST, Reuters

key_facts.fact: Juvmo is the first and only selective D1/D5 receptor agonist approved for adults with Parkinson's, taken once daily with or without levodopa.
key_facts.excerpt: JUVMO is the first and only selective D1/D5 receptor agonist approved for adults with Parkinson's disease. Taken once daily with or without levodopa therapy

key_facts.fact: AbbVie R&D chief Roopal Thakkar called it 'the first dopaminergic breakthrough for Parkinson's disease in decades'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The approval of JUVMO marks the first dopaminergic breakthrough for Parkinson's disease in decades," said Roopal Thakkar, M.D., executive vice president, research and development, chief scientific officer, AbbVie.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 TEMPO-3 trial, Juvmo plus levodopa raised daily 'on' time without troublesome dyskinesia by 1.7 hours versus 0.6 hours on placebo at week 26.
key_facts.excerpt: In TEMPO-3 at week 26, JUVMO 5-15 mg + oral levodopa significantly increased total daily "on" time without troublesome dyskinesia versus placebo + oral levodopa (1.7 hours versus 0.6 hours, p <0.0001).

key_facts.fact: AbbVie expects Juvmo to be available to US patients in October 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: AbbVie expects to make JUVMO available to patients in the U.S. in October 2026.

stories.headline: Russia hits Kyiv data centers as Lavrov vows war 'to the end'; Ukraine reports gains near Lyman

key_facts.fact: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the UN General Assembly on Saturday that Russia intends to continue its military campaign 'to the end'.
key_facts.excerpt: On Saturday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the UN General Assembly his country intended to continue its military campaign "to the end".

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Russia launched more than 2,200 attack drones, about 1,650 aerial bombs and 38 missiles at Ukraine in the past week.
key_facts.excerpt: "This past week, the Russians launched more than 2,200 attack drones against Ukraine, as well as around 1,650 aerial bombs and 38 missiles of various types, a significant number of them ballistic missiles," Zelensky posted

key_facts.fact: Russia's defence ministry said it bombed a Kyivstar data centre in Kyiv and another belonging to Omega Telecom, claiming they served the Ukrainian army; Kyiv was attacked for a third straight day.
key_facts.excerpt: In Moscow, Russia's defence ministry said it had bombed a Kyivstar data centre in Kyiv and another belonging to the Omega Telecom company, claiming that the firms were providing services to the Ukrainian army.

key_facts.fact: Russian attacks killed 14 people and injured 57 across Ukraine over the day, including a 'mass strike' on Odesa Oblast with 170 Shahed-type drones, 76 of them jet-powered.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 14 people were killed and 57 others injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the past day... Russian forces launched 170 Shahed-type attack drones, including 76 jet-powered versions

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Ukrainian forces killed or wounded 10,660 Russian troops this week while advancing in the Lyman sector under Operation 'Vivaldi'.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian Defense Forces have achieved important battlefield results in the Lyman axis in Donetsk region under Operation "Vivaldi," ... Ukrainian units have killed or wounded about 10,660 Russian military personnel across the front this week.

key_facts.fact: ISW assesses Putin is shifting to a theory of victory based on mass jet-powered drone and ballistic strikes to force Ukraine to capitulate over winter 2026-2027; Zelensky put Ukraine's interception rate of jet-powered Shaheds at 55%.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky stated on September 26 that Ukraine's interception rate of jet-powered Shahed drones is now 55 percent, as Ukrainian air defenses intercepted more than 1,500 such drones out of 2,730 that Russia launched in September 2026 thus far.

stories.headline: Defense cyber firm REDLattice to go public via Bold Eagle SPAC at $1.25B valuation

key_facts.fact: REDLattice, a US operational cyber intelligence company serving national security missions, agreed to go public on Nasdaq under ticker 'REDL' by merging with SPAC Bold Eagle Acquisition Corp.
key_facts.excerpt: the leading operational cyber intelligence platform providing integrated technology solutions to support critical national security and intelligence missions, and Bold Eagle Acquisition Corp. ... entered into a definitive agreement for a business combination that would result in REDLattice becoming a publicly traded company listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "REDL"

key_facts.fact: The deal values REDLattice at a pre-money enterprise value of $1.25 billion and should raise up to about $610 million, including $335 million of committed capital.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction values the US-based defense technology company at a pre-money enterprise value of $1.25 billion. The deal is expected to generate proceeds of up to roughly $610 million, including $335 million in committed capital

key_facts.fact: Committed capital comprises $275 million of 4% convertible notes anchored by Loomis Sayles and a $60 million PIPE led by existing investor AE Industrial and Eagle Equity Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: $275 million of convertible notes anchored by Loomis Sayles, featuring a 4% coupon and $12.50 fixed conversion price; and $60 million of common stock PIPE including affiliates of existing investor AE Industrial Partners, LP ("AE Industrial") and Eagle Equity Partners

key_facts.fact: Proceeds will refinance all of REDLattice's debt and fund the final earnout for its Paragon Solutions acquisition; closing is expected around year-end 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Proceeds from the transaction will be used to refinance all of REDLattice's existing debt and to fund the final cash earnout payment from the Company's previously consummated acquisition of Paragon Solutions Ltd.

key_facts.fact: Reuters noted the deal comes as SPACs are making a comeback in the US after years of subdued activity.
key_facts.excerpt: It comes as special purpose acquisition companies (SPACs), an alternative route to public markets, are making a comeback in the US after years of subdued activity.

sources.title: Defense tech firm REDLattice strikes SPAC deal to go public in US

stories.headline: Maritime surveillance startup Quartermaster raises $140M Series B, four months after its Series A

key_facts.fact: Arlington, Virginia-based Quartermaster raised a $140 million Series B after closing a $43 million Series A in May.
key_facts.excerpt: Arlington, Virginia-based startup Quartermaster in May closed a $43 million Series A... Quartermaster has already closed a much larger Series B, bringing in $140 million this time.

key_facts.fact: About $100 million is equity from Insight, new defense-focused investor Overmatch Ventures and existing backers like First Round Capital; the other $40 million is a Stifel debt facility.
key_facts.excerpt: About $100 million of the Series B came from Insight and new investor, defense-focused firm Overmatch Ventures, as well as existing backers like First Round Capital. The remaining $40 million came in the form of a debt facility from investment bank Stifel.

key_facts.fact: Its 'SmartMast' mounts cameras and radios on ship masts to relay real-time maritime data to governments, shippers and insurers, going beyond AIS location pings.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup integrates cameras and radios into a package that's mounted on a ship's mast, and can capture and relay real-time maritime data. This allows governments, shipping companies and insurance providers to know far more than the current standard of AIS

key_facts.fact: More than 650 vessels in 25 countries carry SmartMast, and the company has shipped over 800 units as it prepares fleet-wide deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 650 vessels are now equipped with SmartMast in 25 countries, Sobin said, and the startup has shipped over 800 to customers.

key_facts.fact: Demand has been reinforced by Iran-war-related shipping disruption, and the company has doubled manufacturing capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Demand for its weather-hardened SmartMast sensor network has been reinforced by Iran-war-related shipping disruption... The company has doubled manufacturing capacity
